holidays.name: National Frozen Food Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble freezer aisle. Think frozen peas, pizza rolls, and ice cream sandwiches. The holiday salutes the convenience, and the mild miracle, of dinner that waits patiently for months until you're ready for it.
holidays.origin: The U.S. government recognized the day in 1984. President Ronald Reagan issued a proclamation after lobbying by the frozen food industry.
holidays.funFact: Clarence Birdseye is often called the father of modern frozen food. He got the idea after watching Inuit people in Labrador flash-freeze freshly caught fish in the Arctic air.

holidays.name: National White Chocolate Cheesecake Day
holidays.description: A day for people who think cheesecake needs to be creamier and sweeter. Silky white chocolate swirls into a rich, tangy filling. Raspberry sauce on top is optional, but it is encouraged.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It is part of the long calendar of dessert-themed days that fans share every year.
holidays.funFact: White chocolate has no cocoa solids at all. It is made from cocoa butter, sugar, and milk, so some purists argue it isn't technically chocolate.

holidays.name: National Dentist's Day
holidays.description: A day to thank the people who peer into our mouths and gently scold us about flossing. Celebrate with a thank-you note, a fresh toothbrush, or finally booking that overdue checkup.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It honors dental professionals and the oral health they protect.
holidays.funFact: Toothbrush-like tools date back thousands of years. Ancient civilizations used frayed twigs, known as chew sticks, to clean their teeth.
